page: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration includes 48 virtual CPUs, derived from 24 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The processor features 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside advanced instruction support such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong compute and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics, as well as stress-ng single-core CPU performance. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top 10 percent. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance for small-block read operations and large-block write operations, though large-block read-only bandwidth falls into the average tier. In database and web operations, the server demonstrates strong capabilities, placing in the top 25 percent for PassMark database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. For machine learning tasks, LLM inference speeds for prompt processing with small models reach top-tier levels, while text generation and larger model processing remain in the strong to average ranges.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48ads_v7 provides a high density of memory and local NVMe storage relative to its vCPU count, making it a resource-dense option for workloads that do not require dedicated GPU acceleration. The combination of 384.0 GB of RAM, fast local storage, and strong multi-core performance makes this server highly suitable for memory-intensive applications. Recommended workloads include large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data analytics pipelines, software compilation, and medium-scale language model inference.
